title: 318: Hundred Years' War: A Game of Thrones (Part 1)

sentences.en: Nigel, with one mighty wrench, tore his enemy from the deck and hurled him down upon his back.
sentences.zh: 奈杰尔猛地一拉，将敌人从甲板上拽了下来，重重地摔倒在地。

sentences.en: His own head was whirling, and he felt that his senses were slipping away, but already his hunting knife was out and pointing through the slit in the brazen helmet.
sentences.zh: 他自己则头晕目眩，感觉意识正在模糊，但他的猎刀已经出鞘，正指着那顶黄铜头盔上的缝隙。

sentences.en: Give yourself up, fair sir, said he.
sentences.zh: “投降吧，好汉子，”他说。

sentences.en: The dagger tinkled down upon the deck.
sentences.zh: 那把短剑叮当一声落在了甲板上。

sentences.en: Seamen and archers ran forward to find Nigel half senseless upon his face.
sentences.zh: 水手和弓箭手们跑上前去，发现奈杰尔面朝下半昏迷地躺着。

sentences.en: They drew him off, and a few deft blows struck off the helmet of his enemy.
sentences.zh: 他们把他拉开，几记熟练的重击便击落了他敌人的头盔。

sentences.en: A head, sharp-featured, freckled and foxy red, disclosed itself beneath it.
sentences.zh: 一头面容清秀、长着雀斑、红如狡狐的头发露了出来。

sentences.en: Nigel raised himself on his elbow for an instant.
sentences.zh: 奈杰尔用手肘撑着身体，支吾了片刻。

sentences.en: You are the red ferret, said he.
sentences.zh: “你就是‘红雪貂’，”他说。

sentences.en: So my enemies call me, said the Frenchman with a smile.
sentences.zh: “我的敌人们都这么叫我，”法国人微笑着说。

sentences.en: I rejoice, sir, that I have fallen to so valiant and honourable a gentleman.
sentences.zh: “阁下，我很高兴自己败在了一位如此英勇高尚的绅士手中。”

sentences.en: I thank you, fair sir, said Nigel feebly.
sentences.zh: “谢谢你，好汉子，”奈杰尔虚弱地说。

sentences.en: I also rejoice that I have encountered so debonair a person, and I shall ever bear in mind the pleasure which I have had from our meeting.
sentences.zh: “我也很高兴能遇到如此风度翩翩的人，我将永远铭记我们相遇带来的快乐。”

sentences.en: So saying, he laid his bleeding head upon his enemy's brazen front and sank into a dead faint.
sentences.zh: 说罢，他把血流如注的头靠在敌人黄铜色的胸甲上，昏死过去。

sentences.en: So Tom Holland, that beautiful passage of prose, the introduction of the red ferret in the book Sir Nigel, which you recommended to me,
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆·霍兰德，你向我推荐的那本小说《爵士奈杰尔》中关于“红雪貂”登场的这段绝妙散文，

sentences.en: you regard that as one of the great landmarks in Western literature, don't you?
sentences.zh: 你认为那是西方文学的伟大里程碑之一，对吧？

sentences.en: I'd completely forgotten the red ferret, and I don't know how I could have done.
sentences.zh: 我完全把“红雪貂”这茬给忘了，真不知道我怎么会忘。之

sentences.en: Yeah, so my father read that to me.
sentences.zh: 对啊，我爸以前读给我听过。

sentences.en: It's by Arthur Conan Doyle.
sentences.zh: 作者是阿瑟·柯南·道尔。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And actually, Arthur Conan Doyle thought that Sir Nigel and the other in the same series, the White Company, were better than Sherlock Holmes.
sentences.zh: 而且事实上，阿瑟·柯南·道尔认为《爵士奈杰尔》和同系列的另一部《白衣军团》比《福尔摩斯》还要好。

sentences.en: And I'm sure that from the reading you've just given, the listeners will agree with that verdict.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，听了你刚才的朗读，听众们也会同意这个评价。

sentences.en: Undoubtedly.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: So Sir Nigel culminates in the Battle of Poitiers, the great victory won by the Black Prince, save of the French, when they capture the French king.
sentences.zh: 所以，《爵士奈杰尔》以普瓦捷战役达到高潮，那是黑太子赢得的伟大胜利，除了法国人，当时他们俘虏了法国国王。

sentences.en: And it filled me with a kind of boyish patriotism, all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 这让我充满了某种孩童般的爱国主义情怀，诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: And I became obsessed by the Hundred Years' War.
sentences.zh: 我开始对百年战争着迷。

sentences.en: So it was one of my great kind of childhood enthusiasMs.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我童年时代的伟大爱好之一。

sentences.en: But it was also the subject of another book that I loved as a child, which gave a very different perspective on the 14th century and the Hundred Years' War,
sentences.zh: 但这也是我小时候喜爱的另一本书的主题，它对14世纪和百年战争提供了截然不同的视角，

sentences.en: which was A Distant Mirror by Barbara Tuckman, who was probably best known for her books on
sentences.zh: 那就是巴巴拉·塔克曼的《远方之镜》，她可能最因关于……的书而闻名

sentences.en: First World War, so Guns of August and The Proud Tower.
sentences.zh: 第一次世界大战，也就是《八月炮火》和《骄傲之塔》。

sentences.en: And she cast the Hundred Years' War, unlike Arthur Conan Doyle, as a period of unbelievable suffering.
sentences.zh: 与阿瑟·柯南·道尔不同，她将百年战争描绘成一个充满难以置信苦难的时期。

sentences.en: So marked by gangs of mercenaries and free booters kind of pillaging and destroying, and you've got the Black Death and everything in the background.
sentences.zh: 其特点是雇佣兵团和强盗四处劫掠破坏，背景中还有黑死病和种种灾难。

sentences.en: So for those people who don't know, Tom, the Hundred Years' War, we are in the 14th and then the 15th century, starting in the 14th.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于那些不知道的人来说，汤姆，百年战争，我们身处14世纪然后是15世纪，始于14世纪。

sentences.en: It's England versus France.
sentences.zh: 这是英国对阵法国。

sentences.en: It is the Titanic, certainly for English schoolboys of a certain age, it was the colossal Titanic showdown between these two diametrically opposed chivalric enterprises.
sentences.zh: 这是泰坦尼克号式的对决，对某个年龄段的英国男校学生来说，这绝对是这两个截然相反的骑士企业之间庞大而轰烈的泰坦尼克号式对决。

sentences.en: It's the longest war in European history.
sentences.zh: 这是欧洲历史上最长的战争。

sentences.en: So it's actually, it's not even 100 years, it's actually 116 years from 1337 to 1453.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，它甚至不止100年，从1337年到1453年，实际上是116年。

sentences.en: In Barbara Tuckman's book, she describes how Edward III, who's the English king, and Philip VI, who is the king of France when England and France go to war,
sentences.zh: 在巴巴拉·塔克曼的书里，她描述了英国国王爱德华三世，以及英法开战时的法国国王腓力六世，

sentences.en: that neither could know that they were opening a war that would outlast both of them, that would develop a life of its own, defying parlies and truces and treaties designed to stop
sentences.zh: 他们两个谁也无法预知，自己开启了一场将比他们俩都长寿的战争，它将发展出独立的生命，蔑视旨在阻止它的会谈、休战和条约，

sentences.en: it, that would drag on into their sons' lives and the lives of their grandsons and great-grandsons
sentences.zh: 这场战争将拖延到他们儿子的生命中，孙子们的生命中，曾孙们的生命中，

sentences.en: and great-great-grandsons to the fifth generation, that would bring havoc to both sides
sentences.zh: 以及玄孙们直到第五代的生命中，给双方带来浩劫，

sentences.en: and become, as its damage spread through Europe, the final torment of the closing Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 随着其破坏在欧洲蔓延，它成为了中世纪末期最后的折磨。

sentences.en: Craig, that's a bit bleak, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 克雷格，这有点太黯淡了吧，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So basically, it comes in two halves.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，它分为上下半场。

sentences.en: If you think of it as a football match, the first half, five minutes before, you know, halftime, England basically 10-0 up, and then somehow it ends as a draw.
sentences.zh: 如果你把它想象成一场足球比赛，上半场，你知道，在中场休息前五分钟，英国基本上10比0领先，然后不知怎么地以平局收场。

sentences.en: Then the same thing happens in the second half.
sentences.zh: 接着下半场也发生了同样的事情。

sentences.en: So in this episode, we're going to do the build-up to the Hundred Years' War, and then in three episodes that follow, we're going to do that first half.
sentences.zh: 所以在这一集里，我们将讲述百年战争的酝酿，然后在随后的三集里，我们将讲述那个上半场。

sentences.en: So it features Battle of Crecy, Battle of Poitiers, the collapse of France, and then ultimately
sentences.zh: 所以它包括克雷西战役、普瓦捷战役、法国的崩溃，然后最终

sentences.en: Europe into this kind of maelstrom of violence and horror.
sentences.zh: 欧洲陷入了这种暴力和恐怖的漩涡。

sentences.en: But it's a very dramatic story.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个非常戏剧性的故事。

sentences.en: It's also, Tom, is it not the high point of longbows, the Black Prince, the Red Ferret, chivalric gestures, you know, debonair knights, maidens, tournaments, all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 而且，汤姆，这难道不是长弓、黑太子、“红雪貂”、骑士风度、温文尔雅的骑士、少女、比武大会等等的巅峰吗？

sentences.en: That's all here, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这些都在这里，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this is absolutely, par example, of the kind of the classic medieval war.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对是经典中世纪战争的典范。

sentences.en: So if you like knights, if you like longbows, this is absolutely the series for you.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你喜欢骑士，如果你喜欢长弓，这绝对是适合你的系列。

sentences.en: You might think because France and England fight it for over 100 years, and because today we think of certainly Britain and France as basically being pretty much par, don't we?
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为，因为法兰西和英格兰打了100多年，而且因为今天我们认为英国和法国基本上差不多，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, they're kind of pretty much equal weight.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们的份量差不多。

sentences.en: I mean, that's not at all the case.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，事实根本不是这样的。

sentences.en: And that's why it's so thrilling from an English point of view, is that actually England is a minnow compared to France.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么从英国的角度来看它是如此惊心动魄，因为实际上与法国相比，英格兰只是一个小不点。

sentences.en: So France in the early 14th century is by far the richest country in Europe.
sentences.zh: 所以14世纪初的法兰西是欧洲最富有的国家，远远甩开其他国家。

sentences.en: It's by far the most populous.
sentences.zh: 它是人口最多的，没有之一。

sentences.en: It's got kind of six times the income of England, three times the population.
sentences.zh: 它的收入大约是英国的六倍，人口是英国的三倍。

sentences.en: And there are records of French visitors coming to England, and they're amazed at how small it is.
sentences.zh: 有记录显示，法国访客来到英格兰，他们对英格兰如此之小感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Well, France has got its magnificent cathedrals, and it's, you know, Paris is the largest city in Western Europe, and it's kind of London, and England must feel like a backwater.
sentences.zh: 嗯，法国拥有宏伟的大教堂，而且，你知道，巴黎是西欧最大的城市，而伦敦和英格兰一定让人感觉像个穷乡僻壤。

sentences.en: Anyway, Tom, I took you off, sorry, from you got to tell us about one of your visitors.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，汤姆，我刚才把你带偏了，抱歉，你得给我们讲讲你的其中一位访客。

sentences.en: Well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: So he says how of the four or five regions into which one could divide the kingdom of France, the poorest would offer more revenue, more towns and cities, more knights and squires
sentences.zh: 所以他说，在构成法兰西王国的四五个地区中，最贫穷的一个所提供的税收、城镇、骑士和乡绅，

sentences.en: than the whole of England.
sentences.zh: 也比整个英格兰加起来还要多。

sentences.en: It's the kind of thing that Macron says now.
sentences.zh: 这就有点像马克龙现在说的话。

sentences.en: Well, it is, but the French at that point are entirely justified in looking down at England.
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实是，但当时的法国人完全有理由看不起英格兰。

sentences.en: It pains me to say it, but it's true.
sentences.zh: 虽然说这话让我很痛苦，但这是真的。

sentences.en: Because France is, I mean, it's not just that it's richer and more populous.
sentences.zh: 因为法国不仅更富裕、人口更多，

sentences.en: It's also renowned as the home of chivalry.
sentences.zh: 它还以骑士精神的发源地而闻名。

sentences.en: So it has soft power as well as hard power.
sentences.zh: 所以它既有软实力，也有硬实力。

sentences.en: The king of Bohemia, who's gone blind at the age of 40, but continues to be a great knight, which is very, very red ferret kind of territory.
sentences.zh: 波希米亚国王在40岁时失明了，但仍然是一位伟大的骑士，这非常非常符合“红雪貂”的调性。

sentences.en: Rather than hang out ruling Bohemia, he goes to France because he loves it so much, because he sees this as the true home of chivalry.
sentences.zh: 他没有留在波希米亚统治国家，而是去了法国，因为他太喜欢那里了，因为他认为这是骑士精神真正的发源地。

sentences.en: Everyone's speaking French as their second language.
sentences.zh: 每个人都把法语当成他们的第二语言。

sentences.en: You mentioned the cathedrals, so the Gothic style of cathedrals that we have in England.
sentences.zh: 你提到了大教堂，我们在英格兰拥有的哥特式大教堂风格。

sentences.en: I mean, that comes from France.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是从法国传过来的。

sentences.en: You mentioned Paris, by far the largest city north of the Alps, by far the most prestigious university.
sentences.zh: 你提到了巴黎，阿尔卑斯山以北最大的城市，拥有声望最高的大学。

sentences.en: It has, by medieval standards, a very, very effective civil servants, much more effective than the English one.
sentences.zh: 按中世纪的标准来看，它拥有非常非常高效的公务员队伍，比英国的高效得多。

sentences.en: And so it's, I mean, it's absolutely the gorilla in the room of medieval Christian kingdoms in the early 14th century.
sentences.zh: 所以它，我的意思是，它绝对是14世纪初中世纪基督教王国中的庞然大物。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's the United States in the 1950s or something, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 对，它就像20世纪50年代的美国之类的是吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's just sort of so glittering, so powerful, so modern.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它就是那种光芒四射、如此强大、如此现代的感觉。

sentences.en: So tell me about the kings of France, because they're a kind of slightly peculiar bunch, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 那么跟我讲讲法国的国王们吧，因为他们是一群有点奇特的人，对吧？

sentences.en: It's the dynasty of the Capetians.
sentences.zh: 那是卡佩王朝。

sentences.en: They've been there since, what, 987?
sentences.zh: 他们从什么时候就在那儿了，987年？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I read from your notes.
sentences.zh: 我是从你的笔记里读到的。

sentences.en: So the kings of France can ultimately claim their origin all the way back to Clovis, who's this Frankish warlord who seizes what had been Roman Gaul.
sentences.zh: 所以法国国王最终可以追溯到克洛维，这个占领了罗马高卢的法兰克军阀。

sentences.en: But the current dynasty of kings in France comes to power in 987, as you said.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，法国现任的国王王朝是在987年上台的。

sentences.en: They get elected, a guy called Hugh Capet.
sentences.zh: 他们选出了一个叫于格·卡佩的人。

sentences.en: And what's great for the Capetians, the heirs of Hugh Capet, is that to a degree that's really unparalleled in medieval history, son follows son, follow son, follow son.
sentences.zh: 对卡佩家族、于格·卡佩的继承人们来说最棒的是，在历史（尤其是中世纪历史）中极其罕见的是，儿子接着儿子，接着儿子，接着儿子。

sentences.en: Kind of 14 kings rule in succession.
sentences.zh: 大约14位国王相继统治。

sentences.en: That's great, because it means that you're not kind of slicing and dicing the inheritance, and there are no inheritance battles.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了，因为这意味着你不用去分割遗产，也没有遗产之争。

sentences.en: And what that in turn enables the kings to do is to expand their power.
sentences.zh: 这反过来又让国王们能够扩张他们的权力。

sentences.en: Because what is kind of our understanding of France, say, as a coherent national entity, a nation state,
sentences.zh: 因为我们对法国的理解，比如作为一个连贯的民族实体、一个民族国家，

sentences.en: this doesn't remotely correspond to what France is in the early Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 这与中世纪早期的法兰西完全不相符。

sentences.en: The kings of France in the 11th century, the 12th century, are ruling a tenth of contemporary France.
sentences.zh: 11世纪、12世纪的法国国王统治着当代法国的十分之一。

sentences.en: So they call it the royal domain.
sentences.zh: 所以他们称之为王室领地。

sentences.en: That's where the king has direct rule.
sentences.zh: 那是国王直接统治的地方。

sentences.en: That's around Paris, is it?
sentences.zh: 那是在巴黎周围，对吧？

sentences.en: Around Paris, stretching down to Orléans.
sentences.zh: 围绕着巴黎，一直延伸到奥尔良。

sentences.en: It's really very small.
sentences.zh: 真的非常小。

sentences.en: The rest of it, so that's about nine-tenths, is ruled by his vassals.
sentences.zh: 其余的，也就是大约十分之九，由他的封臣统治。

sentences.en: I mean, they acknowledge his supremacy, but effectively they're independent.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们承认他的至高无上地位，但实际上他们是独立的。

sentences.en: And some of these are very famous because they intrude on English history.
sentences.zh: 其中一些非常著名，因为它们侵入了英国历史。

sentences.en: So most obviously Normandy.
sentences.zh: 最明显的当然是诺曼底。

sentences.en: So that's where William the Conqueror comes from.
sentences.zh: 征服者威廉就是从那里来的。

sentences.en: He's the Duke of Normandy.
sentences.zh: 他是诺曼底公爵。

sentences.en: But also the Duchy of Anjou, that's where Henry II comes from.
sentences.zh: 还有安茹公国，亨利二世就是从那里来的。

sentences.en: Of England.
sentences.zh: 英格兰的。

sentences.en: Henry II of England.
sentences.zh: 英格兰的亨利二世。

sentences.en: And so the Angevin kings, Henry II, Richard I, John,
sentences.zh: 所以金雀花国王们，亨利二世、理查一世、约翰，

sentences.en: I mean, they are ruling as much of France as the French kings are.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们统治的法国领土和法国国王一样多。

sentences.en: So they've got Normandy, they've got Anjou.
sentences.zh: 所以他们拥有诺曼底，拥有安茹。

sentences.zh: 由于亨利二世娶了阿基坦的埃莉诺，他们还得到了阿基坦，这基本上是法国西南部的一大片土地。

sentences.en: But they're under the French king, right?
sentences.zh: 但他们是在法国国王手下，对吧？

sentences.en: They owe him their allegiance or whatever.
sentences.zh: 他们向他效忠之类的。

sentences.en: For some of them, but say not for Aquitaine.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人是，但比方说阿基坦不是。

sentences.en: So Aquitaine is effectively independent.
sentences.zh: 所以阿基坦实际上是独立的。

sentences.en: They acknowledge no overlord.
sentences.zh: 他们不承认任何宗主。

sentences.en: I mean, they recognize that the king of France is the king, but that doesn't mean that they pay homage to him.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们承认法国国王是国王，但这并不意味着他们向他顶礼膜拜。

sentences.en: And that means that France is kind of inherently vociferous.
sentences.zh: 这意味着法国天生就充满分歧。

sentences.en: But over the course of the 13th century, a succession of brilliantly abled kings are able to not only expand the royal domain,
sentences.zh: 但在13世纪期间，一连串能力极其出众的国王不仅能够扩大王室领地，

sentences.en: but also to effectively eliminate focuses of opposition to their rule.
sentences.zh: 而且还能有效地消灭反对他们统治的势力中心。

sentences.en: So the most obvious one, of course, is the Anjou van Kings, Henry II, that dynasty.
sentences.zh: 所以最明显的当然是金雀花国王，亨利二世，那个王朝。

sentences.en: And the guy who gets kicked out, who ends up being called Lackland, is John.
sentences.zh: 被踢出去、最后被称为无地王的家伙是约翰。

sentences.en: So Normandy gets annexed, all the Loire provinces, all that's left is a tiny chunk of what had been Aquitaine.
sentences.zh: 于是诺曼底被吞并了，所有的卢瓦尔省份也是，剩下的只有曾经的阿基坦的一小块地方。

sentences.en: I mean, basically Gascony centered on Bordeaux, a kind of tiny strip of land stretching southwards from Bordeaux.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上是以波尔多为中心的加斯科尼，一小条向南延伸自波尔多的狭长土地。

sentences.en: And that's pretty much all that the kings of England have left of them.
sentences.zh: 这就是英国国王们剩下的全部了。

sentences.en: We talked about the Albigensian Crusade.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论过阿尔比十字军。

sentences.en: In the Cathar podcast, yeah.
sentences.zh: 在关于卡特派的播客里，是的。

sentences.en: So the French kings use that to basically annex directly to their royal domain,
sentences.zh: 所以法国国王利用这一点，基本上将其直接并入他们的王室领地，

sentences.en: Languedoc, Toulouse, all that kind of area.
sentences.zh: 朗格多克、图卢兹以及所有这些地区。

sentences.en: And also brilliantly in the 13th century, the French annex champagne and brie.
sentences.zh: 同样在13世纪，法国人非常出色地吞并了香槟和布里。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So they can have champagne and cheese parties.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就可以开香槟和奶酪派对勒。

sentences.en: Yeah, very nice.
sentences.zh: 对，非常好。

sentences.en: Wine and cheese.
sentences.zh: 红酒加奶酪。

sentences.en: Lovely.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: That's great for the French kings.
sentences.zh: 这对法国国王来说太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So basically, by the start of the 14th century, large chunks of France are directly under the rule of the French kings.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，到14世纪初，法国的大片土地直接处于法国国王的统治之下。

sentences.en: I mean, not all of them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，并非全部。

sentences.en: So there are large principalities.
sentences.zh: 所以还有很大的诸侯领地。

sentences.en: So there's Gascony that we mentioned.
sentences.zh: 比如我们提到的加斯科尼。

sentences.en: That's southweSt.
sentences.zh: 那在西南部。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Remnants of the Duchy of Aquitaine.
sentences.zh: 阿基坦公国的残余部分。

sentences.en: There's Brittany.
sentences.zh: 还有布列塔尼。

sentences.en: There's Flanders, which is part of the French kingdom, what's now Belgium.
sentences.zh: 还有佛兰德斯，它是法兰克王国的一部分，也就是现在的比利时。

sentences.en: So they've got their own dukedom, haven't they?
sentences.zh: 所以他们有自己的公国，对吧？

sentences.zh: 布列塔尼公爵。

sentences.zh: 这就像是一个庞大的……

sentences.en: Well, I was about to say a game of risk, but it's actually obviously a Game of Thrones, Tom.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我本来想说这是一场风险游戏，但显然，汤姆，这分明就是《权力的游戏》。

sentences.en: Yeah, so Game of Thrones is a great parallel.
sentences.zh: 对，所以《权力的游戏》是个极好的类比。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是我们这集节目的主题。

sentences.zh: 如果你想想维斯特洛和各种……

sentences.en: I mean, that's kind of the relationship.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那种关系有点像。

sentences.en: Seven Kingdoms of Westeros.
sentences.zh: 维斯特洛的七大王国。

sentences.en: The Iron Throne.
sentences.zh: 铁王座。

sentences.en: The Iron Throne.
sentences.zh: 铁王座。

sentences.en: So the Iron Throne claims a kind of supremacy over all the Seven KingdoMs.
sentences.zh: 所以铁王座对整个七大王国声称拥有某种至高无上的权力。

sentences.en: And just on the Iron Throne.
sentences.zh: 而且就针对铁王座而言。

sentences.en: So the person who is on, as it were, the Iron Throne, they call him the most Christian king, don't they?
sentences.zh: 所以坐在，可以说是，铁王座上的人，人们称他为最基督教的国王，对吧？

sentences.zh: 他就是美男子腓力。

sentences.zh: 是这样吗，腓力四世？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 他是配得上铁王座的铁血君王吗？

sentences.zh: 他简直就是铁王座的铁血君王，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 他是一位强硬的统治者。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he's king from 1285 to 1314.
sentences.zh: 所以他在1285年至1314年在位。

sentences.en: Whether he's faced by foreign rivals or cash flow problems,
sentences.zh: 无论是面对外国对手还是现金流问题，

sentences.en: I mean, he hits solutions hard.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他解决问题的手段极其强硬。

sentences.en: So actually, he loses a battle to the Flemish infantrymen.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他曾在与佛兰德斯步兵的战役中战败。

sentences.en: And it's called the Battle of the Golden Spurs, because so many Golden Spurs are taken from the defeated knights, and they get hung up.
sentences.zh: 这场战役被称为金马刺战役，因为从战败的骑士身上缴获了数量惊人的金马刺，并将它们挂了起来。

sentences.en: But Philip isn't having any of that.
sentences.zh: 但腓力可不吃这一套。

sentences.en: So he goes in and he smashes up the Flemings, exacts massive reparations, appropriates the city of Lille.
sentences.zh: 于是他亲自出马，粉碎了佛兰德斯人，勒索了巨额赔款，并强占了里尔市。

sentences.en: So this is when Lille becomes part of the royal domain and therefore France in the long run.
sentences.zh: 所以，正是在这个时候，里尔并入了王室领地，从长远来看也就成了法国的一部分。

sentences.en: He expels the Jews from France so he can grab their money.
sentences.zh: 他将犹太人驱逐出法国，以便掠夺他们的财富。

sentences.en: He destroys the Templars, the Knights Templar.
sentences.zh: 他摧毁了圣殿骑士团，即圣殿骑士。

sentences.en: Oh yeah, and he burns that bloke in front of Notre Dame.
sentences.zh: 哦对，他还把那个家伙在巴黎圣母院前烧死了。

sentences.en: Yeah, he does.
sentences.zh: 对，他确实这么做了。

sentences.en: Jacques de Molay, who was the godfather to his son.
sentences.zh: 雅克·德·莫莱，他儿子的教父。

sentences.en: And he's doing this again because he needs the money.
sentences.zh: 他这么做还是因为他需要钱。

sentences.en: So just as he expelled the Jews, he's abolishing the Templars.
sentences.zh: 正如他驱逐犹太人一样，他现在解散了圣殿骑士团。

sentences.en: So he gets their cash.
sentences.zh: 这样他就得到了他们的现金。

sentences.en: And he even has a crack at the Pope.
sentences.zh: 他甚至还敢对教皇下手。

sentences.en: He sends French troops in to basically to bully the Pope on the face of the eighth.
sentences.zh: 他派法国军队去羞辱并霸凌教皇卜尼法斯八世。

sentences.en: And they hold him hostage.
sentences.zh: 他们把他软禁了。

sentences.en: And the Pope is so shocked that he dies.
sentences.zh: 教皇震惊过度，竟然死掉了。

sentences.en: And this sets in train a series of events that culminates in the movement of the papacy from Rome to Avignon, which is not part of the Kingdom of France,
sentences.zh: 这引发了一系列事件，最终导致教廷从罗马迁往阿维尼翁，阿维尼翁不属于法兰西王国，

sentences.en: but obviously, you know, is very much on the doorstep of the French Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 但显然，你知道的，它就紧挨着法兰西王国的门槛。

sentences.en: So, again, there's a sense that the papacy has become French.
sentences.zh: 所以，同样地，人们有一种教皇已经法兰西化的感觉。

sentences.en: And François, who is the great chronicler of the Hundred Years' War, in his account of the conflict at the beginning,
sentences.zh: 而作为百年战争伟大记事者的弗鲁瓦萨尔，在其对冲突开端的记述中，

sentences.en: he describes France under Philippe the Fair as being gorged, contented, strong, its people rich and prospering, and not one of them knew the word war.
sentences.zh: 他将美男子腓力统治下的法国描述为：吃得饱饱的、心满意足的、强大无比的，其人民富庶繁荣，没有一个人知道战争是什么词。

sentences.en: So it's absolutely a golden age.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对是一个黄金时代。

sentences.en: Now, how does this leave the King of England?
sentences.zh: 那么，这让英格兰国王处于什么境地呢？

sentences.en: I was about to say, let's talk about the real heroes of the story now.
sentences.zh: 我正想说，我们现在来聊聊这个故事真正的英雄们吧。

sentences.en: Well, so the Kings of England, who back in the Orgevin period, the time of Henry II and Richard I, had viewed themselves not just as the equals,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以英格兰国王们——在安茹帝国时期、即亨利二世和理查一世的时代，他们曾将自己视为不仅与法兰西国王平等，

sentences.en: but basically superiors of the Kings of France, their horizons are very shrunken because they've lost all their holdings in France.
sentences.zh: 而且基本高居法兰西国王之上——如今他们的眼界大大缩窄了，因为他们在法国的所有领地都丢光了。

sentences.en: And so England in the 13th century has become very marginal.
sentences.zh: 因此，13th世纪的英格兰变得非常边缘化。

sentences.en: So this is King John, Henry III, Henry III is messing around with Simon de Montfort, and then Edward I and II, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是约翰国王、亨利三世，亨利三世在跟西蒙·德·孟福尔胡闹，然后大概就是爱德华一世和二世了。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: These are pretty much the Kings we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是我们所说的那些国王。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Italians will describe them as the little King of England compared to the giant that is the King of France.
sentences.zh: 意大利人会把他们形容为“英格兰小国王”，相比于法兰西国王这个庞然大物而言。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not all bad, I guess, from the English perspective, because obviously having a King who is the King of England and King of vast swathes of France
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从英格兰的角度来看，这也不完全是坏事，因为显然拥有一个既是英格兰国王又拥有法国大片领土的国王，

sentences.en: means that England relatively gets neglected.
sentences.zh: 意味着英格兰相对会被忽视。

sentences.en: So a King of England who really is only just the King, you know, aside from his tiny strip of Gascony, is basically the King of England.
sentences.zh: 所以一个实际上只是纯粹国王的英格兰国王，你知道的，除了他那一小条加斯科尼领地之外，基本上就是英格兰人的国王。

sentences.en: And I think it helps to consolidate a sense of national unity.
sentences.zh: 我认为这有助于巩固民族统一的意识。

sentences.en: So Sir Nigel, I mean, a more modern Nigel would very much applaud this, right?
sentences.zh: 所以奈杰尔爵士——我的意思是，一个更现代的奈杰尔会非常赞同这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: They would say, this is England for the English.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，这就是属于英国人的英国。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Forget the, it's literally little England.
sentences.zh: 忘掉那些，这简直就是小英格兰。

sentences.en: It's like, forget the foreign entanglements.
sentences.zh: 就像是，忘掉那些外国的纠葛吧。

sentences.en: Let's just concentrate on our own sense of national identity and who cares about the French stuff.
sentences.zh: 让我们专注于我们自己的民族认同感，谁管法国那些事。

sentences.en: Is there a bit of an element of that, do you think, developing?
sentences.zh: 你认为这其中是不是也有那么一点这种苗头在发展？

sentences.en: So England as a kingdom that's on an island is geographically more homogeneous.
sentences.zh: 所以作为一个岛国王国，英格兰在地理上更加单一。

sentences.en: But you mentioned Sir Nigel.
sentences.zh: 但你提到了奈杰尔爵士。

sentences.en: I mean, the English are famous throughout Christendom in this period for their xenophobia, their kind of hostility to going abroad.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在这段时期，英国人以其排外心理以及对出国旅行的某种抵触情绪而闻名于整个基督教世界。

sentences.en: And obviously this is true of the mass of the people.
sentences.zh: 显然广大民众确实如此。

sentences.en: The nobility is still very, very attracted to French examples.
sentences.zh: 但贵族阶层仍然非常非常受法国模范的吸引。

sentences.en: But even among them, these are the heirs of people who came over with William the Conqueror.
sentences.zh: 即便在他们之中——这些人是跟随征服者威廉渡海而来的随从的后代——

sentences.en: They're starting to lose French as a first language.
sentences.zh: 他们也开始失去将法语作为第一语言的习惯。

sentences.en: That's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有意思。

sentences.en: And so Frasser, when he's writing about the dealings of English diplomats with the French in the 14th century, I mean, he says that often when the English run into trouble,
sentences.zh: 因此，当弗鲁瓦萨尔在14世纪撰写关于英国外交官与法国人打交道的事情时，我的意思是，他说通常当英国人陷入麻烦时，

sentences.en: they'll pretend that they don't understand what the French are saying.
sentences.zh: 他们会假装听不懂法国人在说些什么。

sentences.en: Increasingly, they have English names.
sentences.zh: 他们越来越多地使用英国名字。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: Edward.
sentences.zh: 爱德华。

sentences.en: Yeah, Edward would be the classic example.
sentences.zh: 对，爱德华就是典型的例子。

sentences.en: Or indeed, Thomas.
sentences.zh: 或者索性叫托马斯。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: A splendid name.
sentences.zh: 一个响亮的名字。

sentences.en: Well, Edward is a really interesting one because that's obviously an Anglo-Saxon name, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，爱德华是一个非常有趣的名字，因为这显然是一个盎格鲁-撒克逊名字，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the kings of England, the Plantagenet kings, are now adopting Anglo-Saxon names.
sentences.zh: 而且英格兰国王、金雀花王朝的国王们现在开始采用盎格鲁-撒克逊名字了。

sentences.en: So they have become Anglicized in a way that they wouldn't have been a few generations earlier.
sentences.zh: 所以他们已经实现了本土化，这是他们在前几代人时所没有的。

sentences.en: They are, although the kings of England are in a way a special case because they do continue to speak French as their first language.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，尽管英格兰国王在某种程度上是一个特例，因为他们确实继续把法语作为他们的第一语言。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And also, they absolutely still see themselves as peers of France and as major continental players.
sentences.zh: 而且，他们绝对依然把自己视作法国的同辈以及欧洲大陆的重要玩家。

sentences.en: So there is something of British prime ministers in the wake of the Second World War still wanting to believe that they are the leaders of a great power, of a superpower.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像第二次世界大战后的英国首相，依然想要相信自己是一个大国、一个超级大国的领袖。

sentences.en: Kings like certainly Edward I are very reluctant to acknowledge their diminished status.
sentences.zh: 像爱德华一世这样的国王绝对非常不愿意承认他们地位的下降。

sentences.en: And to be honest, they certainly have stakes, continuing stakes in France in a way that, say, the French king does not in England.
sentences.zh: 老实说，他们在法国确实拥有利益，并且一直在维系这些利益，而法国国王在英国则没有这样的利益。

sentences.en: So they have stakes in both the two autonomous principalities, Flanders and Brittany.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在两个自治领地——佛兰德斯和布列塔尼——都拥有利益。

sentences.en: So Flanders is the great center of weaving.
sentences.zh: 所以佛兰德斯是伟大的纺织中心。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the weaving depends on English wool.
sentences.zh: 而纺织业依赖于英国的羊毛。

sentences.en: That relationship between England and Flanders, I suppose, Belgium, northern Belgium, is a fascinating one, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 英格兰与佛兰德斯（我猜也就是现在的比利时、北部比利时）之间的这种关系，真是一种令人着迷的关系，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because we did a podcast about Burgundy with Bart van Leeu and he was talking about how in the 15th century there was a sort of almost a natural English-Burgundian alliance.
sentences.zh: 因为我们曾就勃艮第采访过巴特·范·莱乌，他谈到在15世纪时，几乎存在一种天然的英格兰-勃艮第同盟。

sentences.en: Because that economic relationship about wool is so important, does that mean that in this period there's an automatic political relationship as well?
sentences.zh: 既然关于羊毛的这种经济关系如此重要，那是不是意味着在这一时期，也自动存在一种政治关系呢？

sentences.en: I think not for the counts of Flanders and they are counts.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于佛兰德斯伯爵来说并非如此，而且他们是伯爵。

sentences.en: Sorry, I said dukes earlier.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我刚才说的是公爵。

sentences.en: There's so many dukes and counts.
sentences.zh: 有太多的公爵和伯爵了。

sentences.en: It's very confusing.
sentences.zh: 这太容易让人搞混了。

sentences.zh: 那是我的错，汤姆。

sentences.en: I dragged you into a duke morass.
sentences.zh: 是我把你拖进了一个公爵的泥潭里。

sentences.en: The counts of Flanders, they're counts.
sentences.zh: 佛兰德斯的伯爵们，他们是伯爵。

sentences.en: They're not interested in wool and weaving.
sentences.zh: 他们对羊毛和纺织并不感兴趣。

sentences.en: But there's this kind of proto-industrial revolution happening in Flanders.
sentences.zh: 但佛兰德斯正在发生某种准工业革命。

sentences.en: And so the cities that is the home of the weavers are becoming more and more autonomous, more and more significant.
sentences.zh: 因此，作为织工家园的那些城市正变得越来越自治，越来越重要。

sentences.en: That means that the kings of England who supply the raw material are finding that this gives them a way of affecting and influencing opinion in Flanders.
sentences.zh: 这意味着提供原料的英格兰国王发现，这为他们提供了一种影响和左右佛兰德斯舆论的途径。

sentences.en: So they can kind of impose trade blockades.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可以实施某种贸易封锁。

sentences.en: And this is a weapon that over the course of the 13th century into the 14th century, they're not reluctant to use.
sentences.zh: 这是他们在13世纪到14世纪期间毫不犹豫会使用的一种武器。

sentences.en: And so that gives them a point of leverage over Flanders is by far the richest of the various regions of France.
sentences.zh: 因此，这赋予了他们对佛兰德斯的某种杠杆作用，而佛兰德斯是法国各地中最为富裕的。

sentences.en: So that does give them a kind of throttle hold.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实赋予了他们一种扼制咽喉的力量。

sentences.en: They also have a very, the kings of England have a very close relationship with the dukes of Brittany because the brilliantly named Alan of Brittany,
sentences.zh: 他们还与布列塔尼公爵有着非常——英格兰国王与布列塔尼公爵有着非常紧密的关系，因为那个拥有极其响亮名字的布列塔尼的阿兰，

sentences.en: he'd come over with William the Conqueror and been given lands.
sentences.zh: 他曾跟随征服者威廉渡海并被赐予了土地。

sentences.en: And so this is part of inheritance.
sentences.zh: 所以这是遗产的一部分。

sentences.en: One of them is the duke of Brittany is the Earl of Richmond.
sentences.zh: 其中一位布列塔尼公爵同时也是里士满伯爵。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: Richmond is the seat of Rishi Sunak.
sentences.zh: 里士满是里希·苏纳克的选区所在地。

sentences.en: So in Yorkshire.
sentences.zh: 也就是在约克郡。

sentences.en: And the entirety of holdings in England that the dukes of Brittany have probably is giving them a greater income than they're getting from Brittany itself.
sentences.zh: 布列塔尼公爵们在英格兰拥有的全部产业，带给他们的收入可能比他们从布列塔尼本身获得的还要多。

sentences.en: And an example of how intimate the relations between the ducal family of Brittany and the English king is provided by a guy called John, Jean, in the early 14th century,
sentences.zh: 而布列塔尼公爵家族与英格兰国王之间的关系是多么亲密，14世纪初一个叫约翰（让）的人就是一个例子，

sentences.en: who's the uncle of the duke of Brittany in that time.
sentences.zh: 他是当时布列塔尼公爵的叔叔。

sentences.en: But he's also a peer who sits in the House of Lords.
sentences.zh: 但他同时也是一个坐在英国上议院里的贵族同行。

sentences.en: He fights with the English armies against the Scots, actually against the French as well.
sentences.zh: 他曾与英国军队并肩作战对抗苏格兰人，实际上也对抗过法国人。

sentences.en: He's godfather to the future, Edward III.
sentences.zh: 他是未来国王爱德华三世的教父。

sentences.en: So there are absolutely very, very important links there.
sentences.zh: 所以那里绝对存在着非常非常重要的联系。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I think Brittany should still be part of England to be quite frank with you, but that's a niche opinion.
sentences.zh: 坦白对你讲，我认为布列塔尼仍然应该属于英格兰，但这只是个冷门观点。

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: Go on, Tom.
sentences.zh: 继续说，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well, and also just to reiterate, the English kings do have direct holdings.
sentences.zh: 嗯，另外也要重申一遍，英格兰国王确实拥有直接的领地。

sentences.en: So they do have Gascony.
sentences.zh: 所以他们确实拥有加斯科尼。

sentences.en: And also from the time of Edward I, they have this region called Pontieux, which is just south of Calais, which they've kind of inherited by marriage.
sentences.zh: 而且从爱德华一世时期开始，他们还拥有一个叫做蓬蒂约的地区，就在加来正南方，那是他们通过联姻继承来的。

sentences.en: What about Aquitaine?
sentences.zh: 那阿基坦呢？

sentences.en: So Eleanor of Aquitaine, famously, you know, tremendous heiress, brought all these lands, all this money.
sentences.zh: 所以众所周知，阿基坦的埃莉诺是一位了不起的女继承人，带来了所有的这些土地和财富。

sentences.en: Have we still got Aquitaine?
sentences.zh: 我们还占有阿基坦吗？

sentences.en: We have, but very precariously, kind of clinging on with our fingernails, I say our, the English kings are.
sentences.zh: 占有，但非常不稳，可以说是千钧一发，我是说我们，英国国王们是。

sentences.en: Henry III, who's a bit of, to be honest, not the most charismatic and forward thinking of English kings, he basically arrives at a compromise that is in effect a disaster.
sentences.zh: 亨利三世老实说算不上英格兰历代国王中最具个人魅力和远见的一位，他基本上达成了一个实际上堪称灾难的妥协。

sentences.en: So in 1259, he signs a treaty, the Treaty of Paris, which means that the French kings acknowledge their rule over this kind of the rump of what had been Aquitaine, Gascony.
sentences.zh: 所以在1259年，他签署了一项条约，即《巴黎条约》，这意味着法国国王承认他们对阿基坦残余部分也就是加斯科涅的统治。

sentences.en: But in return, Henry III is obliged to pay homage for it.
sentences.zh: 但作为交换，亨利三世必须为此向法王效忠。

sentences.en: This is signed with the aim of establishing kind of concord and peace between the two kings, but it doesn't have that effect because in the long run,
sentences.zh: 签署这个条约的目的是在两位国王之间建立某种和谐与和平，但并没有达到这个效果，因为从长远来看，

sentences.en: and Henry III hadn't realised it, but Edward I, his much more kind of swaggering son, absolutely does.
sentences.zh: 亨利三世没有意识到这一点，但他的儿子爱德华一世，那个气势汹汹得多的儿子，绝对意识到了。

sentences.en: What this means is that his subjects in Gascony can appeal over his head to the French king.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他在加斯科涅的臣民可以越过他直接向法国国王上诉。

sentences.en: So in other words, he's not mastering his own domain.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他无法掌控自己的领地。

sentences.en: And also it's humiliating for a king to pay homage to another king.
sentences.zh: 而且，一个国王向另一个国王效忠也是一种耻辱。

sentences.en: That's absolutely what Edward feels.
sentences.zh: 爱德华正是这种感受。

sentences.en: And so Edward, who is the hammer of the Scots, the guy who conquers Wales,
sentences.zh: 所以爱德华，这位苏格兰的重锤、征服威尔士的人，

sentences.en: I think there's absolutely a sense in which he is looking to expand the borders of England within the island of Britain as a way of compensating for his diminished status on the continent.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他完全有一种试图在不列颠岛内扩大英格兰边界的想法，以此来弥补他在欧洲大陆上日渐衰微的地位。

sentences.en: Oh, that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 哦，这很有意思。

sentences.en: So in other words, the Scot hammering is just a massive form of-
sentences.zh: 换句话说，暴打苏格兰人只是一种大规模的——

sentences.en: Displacement.
sentences.zh: 心理防御机制。

sentences.en: Displacement, yeah.
sentences.zh: 防御机制，没错。

sentences.en: So a couple of questions before we go to a break.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们休息之前，先问几个问题。

sentences.en: Like, presumably, if you're the English king, no matter whether you're Henry III or Edward I or whoever, because France is so rich and so culturally prestigious,
sentences.zh: 比如说，如果你是英格兰国王，不管你是亨利三世、爱德华一世还是别的什么人，由于法国是如此富庶且文化声望如此之高，

sentences.en: you would much prefer to expand your domains in France than to be conquering-
sentences.zh: 你肯定会更愿意在法国扩张领土，而不是去征服——

sentences.en: Scotland.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰。

sentences.en: Yeah, Carnarvon or Edinburgh or whatever.
sentences.zh: 对，卡那封、爱丁堡或是别的什么地方。

sentences.en: You know, it's not just Scotland and Wales, it's England as well.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这不仅关乎苏格兰和威尔士，也关乎英格兰自身。

sentences.en: It's seen as being, well, it's not France.
sentences.zh: 它被视为，嗯，它不是法国。

sentences.en: I mean, who wouldn't want to have a bit of France?
sentences.zh: 我是说，谁不想拥有哪怕一点法国领土呢？

sentences.en: So France is the kind of the metropole, if you like, and these places are peripheral powers.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你愿意的话，法国就相当于大都市，而这些地方则是边缘权力。

sentences.en: It's richer, it's more prosperous, it's more prestigious, and it's the home of chivalry.
sentences.zh: 它更富裕、更繁荣、声望更高，而且是骑士精神的发源地。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And certainly the English kings feel they want to be a part of this.
sentences.zh: 而且英格兰国王们肯定觉得自己也想成为其中的一部分。

sentences.en: They'd much rather have Normandy or Anjou than they would have, say, I don't know, Southern Scotland or Wales or maybe even Surrey.
sentences.zh: 比起比如，我不知道，苏格兰南部、威尔士甚至萨里郡，他们绝对更想要诺曼底或安茹。

sentences.en: Just on the English kings, the English kings think of themselves as English or as French or both?
sentences.zh: 说到英格兰国王，他们觉得自己是英格兰人、法国人，还是两者兼有？

sentences.en: They think of themselves as kings of England, and so they are absolutely identifying themselves, as we will see with the legends of England, of Britain, with King Arthur,
sentences.zh: 他们认为自己是英格兰国王，所以他们绝对认同自己，正如我们将在英格兰、不列颠的传说中以及亚瑟王身上所看到的那样，

sentences.en: all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的一切。

sentences.en: But they see themselves as well as being players in French politics, as being peers of the great figures of the French court.
sentences.zh: 但他们也认为自己是法国政治的参与者，是法国宫廷大人物们的同辈贵族。

sentences.en: So they are absolutely torn, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他们绝对备受拉扯。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't think they'd be conscious of themselves being torn,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不认为他们会意识到自己被拉扯，

sentences.en: because I don't think that they would be thinking that English and French are absolute categories in the way that we would.
sentences.zh: 因为我不认为他们会像我们这样把英格兰和法国视为绝对对立的范畴。

sentences.en: So these are not nation states?
sentences.zh: 所以这些还不是民族国家？

sentences.en: These are not nation.
sentences.zh: 这些不是民族。

sentences.en: I mean, England is much more approximating to a nation state than France is, but this is not really how the kings of England see it, I think.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，英格兰比法国更接近民族国家，但这并不是英格兰国王们真正的看法，我认为。

sentences.en: That question that I just asked, they wouldn't understand the question, because they would say-
sentences.zh: 我刚刚提出的那个问题，他们根本听不懂，因为他们会说——

sentences.en: Probably not.
sentences.zh: 可能听不懂。

sentences.en: You can absolutely be English and French, because French is a sort of different category almoSt.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以既是英国人又是法国人，因为法国几乎是一种完全不同的范畴。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Would that be right?
sentences.zh: 真的是这样吗？

sentences.en: Just like you can be Norman and French, or Breton and French.
sentences.zh: 就像你可以既是诺曼人又是法国人，或者既是布列塔尼人又是法国人一样。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: The mass of people in England think of themselves as English, but the kings of England are operating in a more elevated, more complex,
sentences.zh: 英格兰的广大民众认为自己是英国人，但英格兰国王们的自我认知处于一种更高层次、更复杂、

sentences.en: more historically informed sense of themselves.
sentences.zh: 且具有更多历史积淀的境界中。

sentences.en: They're part of a wider international global elite, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 他们是更广阔的国际全球精英的一部分，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, they're kings, by definition.
sentences.zh: 嗯，从定义上讲他们是国王。

sentences.en: But the tournaments and all that kind of thing, I know this is a stupid comparison.
sentences.zh: 但比武大会和诸如此类的事情，我知道这个比喻可能很蠢。

sentences.en: They are the sort of Davos get-togethers of the day, right?
sentences.zh: 它们就像当年的达沃斯论坛对吧？

sentences.en: They're very rich people go to, and they have a lingua franca, which is French.
sentences.zh: 那是有钱人去的地方，他们有一种通用语，那就是法语。

sentences.en: They move in a different kind of cultural universe from the people that they rule.
sentences.zh: 他们生活在一种与他们所统治的人民截然不同的文化世界里。

sentences.en: So rather than kind of meeting up and talking about what does AI mean for global finance, they would compete in the lists, tournaments, all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不会聚在一起讨论人工智能对全球金融意味着什么，而是会在比武场上竞技、举办比武大会以及做所有这些事情。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: One other thing I want to talk about, which is wine.
sentences.zh: 我还要谈另一件事，那就是葡萄酒。

sentences.en: So you mentioned, oh, we still have Gascony.
sentences.zh: 所以你提到，哦，我们还拥有加斯科涅。

sentences.en: We still have Bordeaux.
sentences.zh: 我们还拥有波尔多。

sentences.en: So presumably wine is quite a big factor in all this, is it?
sentences.zh: 所以想必葡萄酒在这其中是一个相当大的因素，对吗？

sentences.en: The wine trade must be significant.
sentences.zh: 葡萄酒贸易一定很重要。

sentences.en: We are importing claret or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我们在进口红葡萄酒或是别的什么。

sentences.en: Is that why the obsession with Bordeaux in England?
sentences.zh: 这就是英格兰对波尔多如此执着的原因吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's about 80,000 tons of wine are being exported annually to England.
sentences.zh: 每年大约有8万吨葡萄酒被出口到英格兰。

sentences.en: And so, again, that gives incredible leverage.
sentences.zh: 所以，同样地，这提供了极大的筹码。

sentences.en: So the two kind of great export industries of France, the Flemish wool and the wines of Bordeaux are both absolutely intimately fused with England.
sentences.zh: 因此，法国的两个伟大出口产业，佛兰德斯的羊毛和波尔多的葡萄酒，都与英格兰完全紧密地融为一体。

sentences.en: But it's an unstable relationship because of this issue of the paying homage and because of the power imbalance between the two and because of the aspirations of the – because the French court obviously has an aspiration to kind of spread French power over France.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种不稳定的关系，因为效忠的问题，因为两者之间的权力不对等，以及因为——因为法国宫廷显然有一种在法国全境扩展法国权力的渴望。

sentences.en: And the English kings have an aspiration to preserve and indeed widen their own –
sentences.zh: 而英格兰国王则渴望维护甚至扩大他们自己的——

sentences.en: Claw it back.
sentences.zh: 夺回失地。

sentences.en: So that's the basic instability, would you say, the aspirations of the rival courts.
sentences.zh: 所以你认为，这就是根本的不稳定性所在，即敌对宫廷各自的野心。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, we should take a break, I think, Tom.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想我们该休息一下了，汤姆。

sentences.en: And I believe we're going to come back in with one of my very favourite English kings.
sentences.zh: 而且我相信我们回来后会讲到我最喜欢的英格兰国王之一。

sentences.en: Not a good king, it's fair to say, but an interesting king because we're going to come back in with Edward II.
sentences.zh: 虽说不上是个好国王，但却是个有趣的国王，因为我们要讲的是爱德华二世。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Described by one of his biographers in 1900 as an absolute ninny.
sentences.zh: 1900年被他的一位传记作家描述为绝对的笨蛋。

sentences.en: An absolute ninny.
sentences.zh: 一个绝对的笨蛋。

sentences.en: We're going to return with an absolute ninny, Edward II.
sentences.zh: 我们将带着一个绝对的笨蛋——爱德华二世回归。

sentences.en: So come back after the break.
sentences.zh: 所以休息之后见。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的剩余部分》。

sentences.en: We promised you we would return with King Edward II.
sentences.zh: 我们向大家保证过，我们将带着爱德华二世国王回归。

sentences.en: And we have – Tom has just said to me in the break, tell everybody about Edward II because clearly he doesn't know anything about him.
sentences.zh: 我们已经——汤姆刚才在休息时对我说，给每个人讲讲爱德华二世吧，因为他显然对这个人一无所知。

sentences.en: So, Tom, to educate you and the audience, Edward II was a useless king.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，为了启迪你和听众，爱德华二世是个废物国王。

sentences.en: Doesn't he appear in Braveheart?
sentences.zh: 他没有出现在《勇敢的心》里吗？

sentences.en: He's in Braveheart, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他在《勇敢的心》里，对吧？

sentences.en: It's Cook Old Ed by William Wallace.
sentences.zh: 那是威廉·华莱士对娘娘腔老爱德华的称呼。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 他确实在。

sentences.en: He's married to Sophie Marceau in Braveheart.
sentences.zh: 他在《勇敢的心》里娶了苏菲·玛索。

sentences.en: In reality, he is indeed beaten at the Battle of Bannetburn in Scotland, Edward II.
sentences.zh: 现实中，爱德华二世确实在苏格兰的班诺克本战役中被打败了。

sentences.en: So his father of the first is an incredibly formidable fellow, the Hammer of the Scots.
sentences.zh: 所以他的父亲一世是一个极其可怕的人物，苏格兰的重锤。

sentences.en: Edward II, useless, great domestic instability at home.
sentences.zh: 爱德华二世是个废物，国内政局极度动荡。

sentences.en: There's all these favourites, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 有各种各样的宠臣，对吧？

sentences.en: Endless favourites.
sentences.zh: 没完没了的宠臣。

sentences.en: Waves of them.
sentences.zh: 一波又一波。

sentences.en: This is very 266 and all that.
sentences.zh: 这非常符合《1066及其所有》的风格。

sentences.en: There's the dispensers.
sentences.zh: 有德斯潘瑟家族。

sentences.en: There's obviously noisatoriously Piers Gaveston with whom he was supposed to have been infatuated.
sentences.zh: 当然还有臭名昭著的皮尔斯·加夫斯顿，据说他曾对这个人迷恋不已。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Edward II's weakness.
sentences.zh: 还有爱德华二世的软弱。

sentences.en: Now, why is that a problem?
sentences.zh: 现在，为什么这会是个问题呢？

sentences.en: Why does that destabilise things?
sentences.zh: 为什么这会破坏局势稳定？

sentences.en: Because obviously, from the French point of view, I mean, that's great that he's so weak.
sentences.zh: 因为很显然，从法国的角度来看，他这么软弱当然是件好事。

sentences.en: Why would that change the relationship between England and France, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，为什么这会改变英格兰和法国之间的关系？

sentences.en: So Scotland has, since 1295, been in alliance with France.
sentences.zh: 所以自1295年以来，苏格兰一直与法国结盟。

sentences.en: This is the old alliance.
sentences.zh: 这就是老同盟。

sentences.en: And so his priority basically is to repudiate that.
sentences.zh: 所以他的首要任务基本上就是废除那个条约。

sentences.en: And he does this by, you remember John Balliol, who was originally the king of Scotland, appointed by Edward I.
sentences.zh: 他是这样做的：还记得最初由爱德华一世任命的苏格兰国王约翰·巴里奥吗？

sentences.en: His son wants to go and reclaim the throne.
sentences.zh: 他的儿子想要去夺回王位。

sentences.en: And so Edward turns a blind eye when John Balliol's son invades Scotland from Northumbria, take it with a band of adventurers.
sentences.zh: 因此，当约翰·巴里奥的儿子带着一帮冒险者从诺森布里亚入侵苏格兰时，爱德华睁一只眼闭一只眼。

sentences.en: And he does tremendously well.
sentences.zh: 而且他干得极其出色。

sentences.en: And his aim basically is to topple the five-year-old son of Robert Bruce, David II.
sentences.zh: 他的基本目标是推翻罗伯特·布鲁斯的五岁儿子大卫二世。

sentences.en: And it goes very well to begin with.
sentences.zh: 一开始进展非常顺利。

sentences.en: And then it goes very badly.
sentences.zh: 然后情况急转直下。

sentences.en: And by 1333, a large Scottish army have arrived on the banks of the Tweed and are besieging
sentences.zh: 到1333年，一支庞大的苏格兰军队抵达特威德河畔，正在围攻

sentences.en: Berwick.
sentences.zh: 贝里克。

sentences.en: So Edward III goes rushing up to the rescue because he's able to cast this as an invasion of England.
sentences.zh: 因此爱德华三世急忙赶去救援，因为他能把这包装成是对英格兰的入侵。

sentences.en: And he meets with the Scottish army at a place called Halladon Hill, which is a few miles from where Sadie was inherited from her father.
sentences.zh: 他在一个叫哈利登山的地方遇到了苏格兰军队，那里离萨迪从她父亲那里继承遗产的地方只有几英里。

sentences.en: A bonny cottage on the banks of the Tweed.
sentences.zh: 一座坐落在特威德河畔的美丽小屋。

sentences.en: From the Holland country estate, Tom, as I like to think of.
sentences.zh: 来自霍兰乡村庄园，汤姆，我是这么认为的。

sentences.en: It's in our country estate.
sentences.zh: 它在我们国家的庄园里。

sentences.en: And I'm ashamed to say I've never actually visited the site of the Battle of Halladon Hill and I'll be doing it the next time we go up there.
sentences.zh: 我很惭愧地说，我实际上从来没有参观过哈利登山战役的遗址，下次我们上去的时候我一定要去看看。

sentences.en: Anyway, it's an absolutely zinging victory.
sentences.zh: 总之，这是一场绝对震撼的胜利。

sentences.en: Edward absolutely crushes it.
sentences.zh: 爱德华完完全全地大获全胜。

sentences.en: David II has to escape to France.
sentences.zh: 大卫二世不得不逃往法国。

sentences.en: And this absolutely poisons Anglo-French relations because by the terms of the Scottish-French agreement, Philip VI has to back David II and get him back on the throne.
sentences.zh: 这彻底毒化了英法关系，因为根据苏法协议的条款，腓力六世必须支持大卫二世并让他重登王位。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 理所当然。

sentences.en: So this is very provocative to the French.
sentences.zh: 所以这对法国人来说极具挑衅性。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so English ambassadors are, in fact, the Archbishop of Canterbury, are in Paris at the time when David II arrives in France asking for French support.
sentences.zh: 因此，当大卫二世抵达法国寻求法国支持时，英国大使——实际上就是坎特伯雷大主教——当时正在巴黎。

sentences.en: Well, he's not because he's five, but the guys have gone with him.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他自己没去，因为他才五岁，但那些随从去了。

sentences.en: And so Philip VI informs the English ambassadors that there will be no treaty between England and France unless Scotland is included and Scottish rights are upheld.
sentences.zh: 因此，腓力六世通知英国大使，除非把苏格兰包含在内并维护苏格兰的权利，否则英法之间不会有任何条约。

sentences.en: So it's actually very Brexit.
sentences.zh: 所以这其实非常“英国脱欧”。

sentences.en: It's very Brexit, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这太“英国脱欧”了，汤姆。

sentences.en: The equivalent of the Northern Ireland Protocol is getting in the way of an Anglo-French treaty.
sentences.zh: 这就相当于《北爱尔兰议定书》正阻碍着一项英法条约的签署。

sentences.en: And so essentially, Edward III is faced with the choice of abandoning his Scottish claim
sentences.zh: 因此，从本质上讲，爱德华三世面临着放弃他对苏格兰的主张

sentences.en: or risking the security of Gascony.
sentences.zh: 还是冒着危及加斯科尼安全的抉择。

sentences.en: Because obviously, if no treaty is signed with the French king, then the French will feel that they have the right to go and appropriate Gascony.
sentences.zh: 因为很明显，如果没有与法国国王签署条约，法国人就会觉得自己有权去侵占加斯科尼。

sentences.en: So it's a very difficult decision that he has to make.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常艰难的决定，他必须做出抉择。

sentences.en: But because he's an absolute lad, he refuses to compromise.
sentences.zh: 但由于他是个绝对的硬汉，他拒绝妥协。

sentences.en: And so essentially, he says, well, I'm going to uphold my claims on Scotland.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上他说，好吧，我要坚持我对苏格兰的主张。

sentences.en: If you attack Gascony, I'm going to go to war over it.
sentences.zh: 如果你攻击加斯科尼，我就为此发动战争。

sentences.en: And relations between England and France go into a kind of downward spiral.
sentences.zh: 英法关系陷入了一种向下的螺旋。

sentences.en: So by 1336, so that's two years after the Scottish king has fled to France, the whole of England is having a massive invasion scare.
sentences.zh: 因此到了1336年，也就是苏格兰国王逃往法国两年后，整个英格兰都陷入了巨大的入侵恐慌中。

sentences.en: They're kind of building beacons.
sentences.zh: 他们开始修建烽火台。

sentences.en: They're trying to kind of rustle up ships to defend the channel, all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们试图四处搜罗船只来保卫海峡，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And the French kings, meanwhile, is drawing up this incredibly complicated and, in the long run, abortive plan to invade England through Scotland.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，法国国王正在制定一项极其复杂且从长远来看流产了的计划，企图通过苏格兰入侵英格兰。

sentences.en: I mean, which is kind of mad.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有点疯狂。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a very complicated way of doing it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一种非常复杂的操作方式。

sentences.en: So that's looking very, very bad for Edward, the threat of direct invasion.
sentences.zh: 所以，面临直接入侵的威胁，对爱德华来说情况看起来非常非常糟糕。

sentences.en: And then in May 1337, Philip declares that he is confiscating the Duchy of Aquitaine.
sentences.zh: 然后在1337年5月，腓力宣布他要没收阿基坦公国。

sentences.en: And this effectively is a declaration of war.
sentences.zh: 这实际上就是宣战。

sentences.en: Right, because Edward has to respond to that.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为爱德华必须对此作出回应。

sentences.en: Well, so Edward goes to parliament, gets the backing of parliament, gets all the peers of England on side.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以爱德华去见了议会，得到了议会的支持，把英格兰所有的贵族都拉到了自己这边。

sentences.en: So he's absolutely making sure that he's not just treating this as a personal dynastic war.
sentences.zh: 所以他绝对在确保自己不仅仅是把这当作一场个人的王朝战争。

sentences.en: He's making sure that he's getting the peers and the parliament of England on side as well.
sentences.zh: 他确保自己也赢得了英格兰贵族和议会的支持。

sentences.en: And on the 28th of August, 1337, he issues a public manifesto in which he accuses Philip
sentences.zh: 在1337年8月28日，他发表了一份公开宣言，在宣言中他指责腓力

sentences.en: of provoking war by supporting the Scots in defiance of his rights in Scotland, of supporting
sentences.zh: 挑起战争，因为他支持苏格兰人，无视其在苏格兰的权利；支持

sentences.en: French ships in their kind of piratical raids on the English coast, and of behaving unlawfully in stripping him of his ancestral rights in Aquitaine.
sentences.zh: 法国船只在英国海岸进行海盗式的袭击；并且行为不合法，剥夺了他在阿基坦的祖传权利。

sentences.en: So it's really interesting that he feels the need to issue a public manifesto, that this
sentences.zh: 所以非常有趣的是，他觉得有必要发表一份公开宣言，在这样一个

sentences.en: is an age, because the stereotype of the Hundred Years' War is this is just knights and barons among themselves.
sentences.zh: 时代——因为对百年战争的刻板印象是这只是骑士和男爵们之间的事。

sentences.en: But he feels he needs to get the commons, the- He absolutely does.
sentences.zh: 但他觉得他需要争取平民，他——他绝对是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So why is that, do you think?
sentences.zh: 所以你认为这是为什么？

sentences.en: It's in part because Edward can recognise that English identity is something more coherent, say, than French identity, and that if he can rally the mass of the English to a sense
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于爱德华认识到，英国人的认同感比法国人的认同感更具凝聚力，如果他能动员广大英国民众让他们感到

sentences.en: that his cause is England's cause, then obviously that'll be great.
sentences.zh: 他的事业就是英格兰的事业，那么这显然会很棒。

sentences.en: And the reason that he is aware of the need to do that is that Edward knows he has a secret
sentences.zh: 他之所以意识到有必要这样做，是因为爱德华知道他有一个秘密

sentences.en: weapon in the form of an incredible new military technology, which he had actually unleashed at the Battle of Hallidon Hill against the Scots.
sentences.zh: 武器，形式是一种令人难以置信的新军事技术，他实际上已经在哈利登山战役中对苏格兰人使用过了。

sentences.en: And so he knows it's devastating, which is the longbow.
sentences.zh: 所以他知道那是极具毁灭性的，也就是长弓。

sentences.en: And we should probably save that for a discussion in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我们或许应该把这留到下一集的讨论中。

sentences.en: But just to reiterate, Edward's declaration of war, his readiness to uphold his rights against the French monarchy is very, very punchy.
sentences.zh: 但重申一下，爱德华的宣战，他准备捍卫自己对抗法国君主的权利，是非常非常强硬的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's equivalent, say, of in the buildup to the Ukraine war, if Ukraine had basically gone to war with Russia and invaded Russia.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这相当于在乌克兰战争爆发前夕，如果乌克兰基本上对俄罗斯开战并入侵了俄罗斯。

sentences.en: It's that level of punchiness.
sentences.zh: 就是那种级别的强硬。

sentences.en: So it's the smaller than the underdog, just saying, right, let's go for it.
sentences.zh: 所以这比弱者还要弱，却说，好吧，我们上吧。

sentences.en: Let's get stuck in.
sentences.zh: 大干一场。

sentences.en: I'm not waiting to be attacked by the bigger dog, as it were.
sentences.zh: 我才不会等着被那只更大的狗攻击呢。

sentences.en: And Edward's strategy is absolutely to take the war to France.
sentences.zh: 爱德华的战略绝对是把战争打到法国本土去。

sentences.en: So in other words, he knows that if the French get a toehold in England, then their capacity to devastate England will be overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他知道如果法国人在英格兰站稳脚跟，那么他们毁灭英格兰的能力将是压倒性的。

sentences.en: But that if he can clear French control of the channel and establish permanent footholds in France and take the war to France, then that will keep England secure from the war.
sentences.zh: 但如果他能清除法国对海峡的控制，在法国建立永久的据点并将战争带到法国，那么这将确保英格兰免受战争侵害。

sentences.en: So that is basically its strategy.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上就是他的战略。

sentences.en: But it's still very, very punchy.
sentences.zh: 但这仍然非常非常强硬。

sentences.en: And the question that people are asking as the war begins isn't, can he win?
sentences.zh: 战争开始时人们问的问题并不是，他能赢吗？

sentences.en: It isn't, can he make himself king of France?
sentences.zh: 不是，他能让自己成为法国国王吗？

sentences.en: It's how can he avoid a French evasion?
sentences.zh: 而是他如何能避免法国人的入侵？

sentences.en: How can he avoid the conquest of Gascony and maybe even England?
sentences.zh: 他如何能避免加斯科尼甚至可能是英格兰被征服？

sentences.en: And basically, pretty much everyone in Europe is expecting him to lose.
sentences.zh: 基本上，欧洲几乎所有人都预料他会输。

sentences.en: Crikey.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: What a dramatic moment on which to end, Tom.
sentences.zh: 以多么戏剧性的时刻结束啊，汤姆。

sentences.en: Because this is just the first of four podcasts, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为这只是四个播客中的第一个，对吧？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 正是。

sentences.en: Arrested History Club members who are interested in longbows, underdog victories, stories of tremendous heroism against overwhelming evil.
sentences.zh: “历史俱乐部”中对长弓、弱者逆袭、在压倒性邪恶面前展现惊人英雄主义的故事感兴趣的会员们。

sentences.en: Black princes, red ferrets.
sentences.zh: 黑太子，红雪貂。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They can listen to the rest of the episodes now.
sentences.zh: 他们现在就可以收听剩下的剧集了。

sentences.en: Ordinary listeners.
sentences.zh: 普通听众。

sentences.en: I mean, there's nothing bad about being ordinary, if that's what you want to be.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，做个普通人没什么不好的，如果你想成为那样的话。

sentences.en: A long moment rather than a night.
sentences.zh: 一段漫长的时光，而不是一个夜晚。

sentences.en: They can.
sentences.zh: 他们可以。

sentences.en: Well, they'll have to wait till Thursday, basically.
sentences.zh: 好吧，基本上他们得等到星期四。

sentences.en: But you can listen now by signing up at restishistorypod.com.
sentences.zh: 但你现在就可以通过在 restishistorypod.com 注册来收听。

sentences.en: And let me tell you one more thing that you will be getting if you do that.
sentences.zh: 让我再告诉你一件事，如果你这样做将会得到什么。

sentences.en: You will get, with each episode, a lovely reading from Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's Sir Nigel, because that's how we'll be introducing future episodes to this series.
sentences.zh: 每集节目中，你都会听到一段对亚瑟·柯南·道尔爵士的《爵士奈杰尔》的美妙朗读，因为这就是我们将本系列未来节目的引子的方式。

sentences.en: So you'll get a taste, not just of great history, courtesy of Tom Holland, but a fantastic high level literary craftsmanship, courtesy of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle and me.
sentences.zh: 所以你不仅能领略到由汤姆·霍兰带来的伟大历史的韵味，还能领略到由亚瑟·柯南·道尔爵士和我带来的极高水平的文学造诣。

sentences.en: So on that bombshell, Tom, we return next time with the Longbow.
sentences.zh: 带着这个重磅消息，汤姆，我们下次带着长弓回归。

sentences.en: What battle have we got coming up?
sentences.zh: 我们接下来要打什么战役？

sentences.en: We've got the Battle of Sluice, which is a great naval victory.
sentences.zh: 我们要讲斯鲁伊斯战役，这是一场伟大的海上大捷。

sentences.en: We've got the Battle of Cressy, which is absolutely brilliant.
sentences.zh: 我们要讲克雷西战役，绝对精彩绝伦。

sentences.en: Basically, it's the medieval Battle of Trafalgar.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这就是中世纪的特拉法加海战。

sentences.en: And we've got the Capture of Calais by the English.
sentences.zh: 我们还要讲英国人攻占加来。

sentences.en: And loads of gallantry, knights, maidens, red ferrets, you name it.
sentences.zh: 还有无数的骑士精神、骑士、少女、红雪貂，应有尽有。

sentences.en: I mean, basically, if you're French, you won't want to listen to it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上，如果你是法国人，你肯定不想听。

sentences.en: But if you're English, you definitely will.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是英国人，你绝对会想听。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Since we don't have any French listeners, who cares?
sentences.zh: 既然我们没有法国听众，谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: And on that bombshell, we'll see you next time.
sentences.zh: 带着这个重磅消息，我们下期再见。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史的余烬》（The Rest is History）。

sentences.zh: 获取独家单集、抢先收听、无广告体验以及加入我们的聊天社区，请在 restishistorypod.com 注册。

sentences.zh: That's restishistorypod.com.
